selfHost.title: Run Guidon on your own server
selfHost.description: The same app, on infrastructure you control: Docker Compose with a plain PostgreSQL, local file storage and optional local AI (Ollama). No plan limits on your own install.

landing.heroShotAlt: Guidon dashboard: your open and overdue tasks, what's next, recent team activity and project progress

items.a: Guidon is a project board for teams. Every project has a Kanban board and, next to it, the decisions behind the work, the sources and technologies it relies on, a roadmap and a project memory - so whoever picks up a task also gets the reason it exists. AI is optional: you can connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex and other apps, and they work from the same tasks under your review.

Yes, there is a free plan. Paid plans on Guidon Cloud raise the limits on projects, members and AI use; they are billed monthly or yearly and start with a 14-day free trial. Self-hosted Guidon has no limits at all.

items.q: Can AI agents work on my tasks?
items.a: Yes. Create a free Guidon account, then generate an API key yourself in Profile > API keys, or connect an MCP client with OAuth. Guidon has a free plan and an example-task sandbox, so you can test the integration without a sales call. The agent finds a task, reads its full context, claims it, records what it tried and hands the work back to a person for review.
Yes. Guidon is open source on GitHub and runs on your own server with plain PostgreSQL. The self-hosting guide walks through the setup.

items.q: How can I try the API without touching real work?
items.a: Create a sandbox: a separate organization with example tasks that you can change freely and reset to the starting data with one request or one click.

items.q: Does Guidon work with game engines?
items.a: Yes. There are plugins for Unity, Unreal Engine, Godot and Blender, in-game bug reports that land on the board, and Guidon Desktop for Windows, macOS and Linux.

items.q: Can I delete my account and data?
items.a: Yes, at any time: Profile → Delete account on the website. The Privacy Policy explains what is stored and why.

descriptions.unity: One package: your project's board and moodboard inside the Unity editor, plus in-game bug reports that land on that board.
descriptions.unreal: One plugin: the task board and moodboard as editor tabs, plus in-game bug reports from Blueprints or C++.
descriptions.godot: One add-on: a task board, moodboard and bug-report panel in the editor, plus in-game bug reports.
descriptions.blender: Task board in the 3D viewport sidebar (N panel).
descriptions.vscode: Task board in the VS Code sidebar. Download the source and build a .vsix.
descriptions.jetbrains: Task board tool window for IntelliJ IDEA, Rider, PyCharm, WebStorm and other JetBrains IDEs. Download the source and build it with Gradle.

unity.s1: Unzip and copy the Guidon folder anywhere under Assets/ (delete GuidonTasks and GuidonReports if you had them).
unity.s2: Open Window → Guidon → Tasks, set Base URL to {baseUrl} and click Log In.
unity.s3: Bug reports: click Reports in the board's toolbar, then Set Up In-Game Reports - the key is created and saved for you.

unreal.s1: Unzip into your project's Plugins/ folder, or run install.ps1 from the Guidon folder (it also removes the old GuidonTasks/GuidonReports plugins).
unreal.s2: Reopen the project and let the editor build the modules - a C++ project is required.
unreal.s3: Open the Guidon Tasks tab, set Base URL to {baseUrl} and click Log In. Reports in its toolbar sets up in-game bug reports.

godot.s1: Unzip into your project's root folder - the files land in addons/guidon (delete addons/guidon_tasks and addons/guidon_reports if you had them).
godot.s2: Enable Guidon in Project → Project Settings → Plugins.
godot.s3: In the Guidon panel, set Base URL to {baseUrl} and click Log In. Reports in its toolbar sets up in-game bug reports.

blender.s1: Don't unzip - Blender installs the zip as it is.
blender.s2: Blender 4.2+: Preferences → Get Extensions → ⌄ → Install from Disk. Blender 3.6-4.1: Preferences → Add-ons → Install.
blender.s3: Allow Online Access in Preferences → System → Network, then set Base URL to {baseUrl} in the N panel and click Log In.

vscode.s1: Unzip, then run npm install, npm run build and npm run package in the folder.
vscode.s2: In VS Code: Extensions → ⋯ → Install from VSIX… and pick the generated file.
vscode.s3: Open the Guidon view, set Base URL to {baseUrl} and click Log In.

jetbrains.s2: Settings → Plugins → ⚙ → Install Plugin from Disk… and pick the zip from build/distributions/.
jetbrains.s3: Open the Guidon tool window, set Base URL to {baseUrl} and click Log In.

onboarding.starterTask_memory_title: Agent: write down what this project is
onboarding.starterTask_memory_description: Read the repository (README, main folders, config files) and save 3-5 facts about this project in Guidon's project memory with create_memory: what it is, the stack, how to run it and how to test it. Then record_attempt and move this task to Review.
onboarding.starterTask_plan_description: Look at the code and the open tasks on this board. Create up to 5 concrete tasks in To do with create_task, each with a short description and a clear "done when". Don't start them - a person picks what comes next. Then move this task to Review.
onboarding.starterTask_improve_title: Agent: make one small, safe improvement
onboarding.starterTask_improve_description: Pick one small improvement you can finish in a few minutes (a typo, a missing README section, an unclear error message). Do it on a new branch, record_attempt with the files you changed, summarize it with comment_on_task and move this task to Review.
onboarding.starterRule: Agents move finished tasks to Review, never straight to Done - a person checks the work first.
